args: In harfbuzz/src/hb-vector.hh, analyze hb_vector_t::alloc() when transitioning from static_array to heap storage. Given that it byte-copies Type elements and static_array elements are later implicitly destructed, what relocation/ownership convention does this old HarfBuzz codebase use, and is clearing the source static_array after memcpy the compatible root fix? Please identify any nearby lifecycle assumptions or analogous transfer patterns in the C++ source.

The sanitizer report shows a double-free for hb_vector_t<CFF::cff1_font_dict_values_t,8>, whose early inline element contains a heap-backed nested hb_vector_t<CFF::op_str_t,8>. At alloc line 166 the outer vector memcpy-copies inline elements into calloc'd heap storage, leaving the source nested vector pointer alive. CFF fini_deep frees the heap copy's nested allocation, then the outer vector object's static_array member destructors run and the stale source alias frees it again. The existing vector uses calloc/realloc and raw memset rather than placement-new or conventional C++ move construction, and fini() only frees arrayZ_, so I suspect its intended convention is bitwise relocation and that the source bytes must be zeroed after a successful inline-to-heap copy. I want confirmation against project idioms before patching harfbuzz/src/hb-vector.hh.
